summary: No pair was identified as a true CMS-policy false suppression. These are specific combinations surgeons may commonly document/report and may be confused by because real work is selected but not separately payable.

pairs.column1Description: Enterectomy, resection of small intestine; single resection and anastomosis
pairs.concern: Small bowel resection with extensive adhesiolysis is commonly documented by surgeons; Medicare NCCI modifier-0 still suppresses 44005, so the UI must emphasize selected/performed vs payable.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.concern: Colectomy with lysis of adhesions is a common operative-note combination; surgeons may expect effort credit, but 44005 is not separately payable under this modifier-0 relationship.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Colectomy, partial; with end colostomy and closure of distal segment (Hartmann type procedure)
pairs.concern: Hartmann procedure often involves adhesiolysis in reoperative abdomen; likely reported by surgeons, but should be suppressed for payable wRVU.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Closure of enterostomy, large or small intestine; without resection and anastomosis
pairs.concern: Ostomy reversal frequently involves adhesiolysis; common user-confusion risk because 44005 work feels real but is bundled.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Closure of enterostomy, large or small intestine; with resection and anastomosis other than colorectal
pairs.concern: Ostomy reversal with resection/anastomosis plus adhesiolysis is clinically plausible and commonly documented; NCCI still suppresses separate 44005 payable credit.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.concern: Ostomy creation with adhesiolysis can be clinically real; risk is surgeon frustration if they think the work disappeared.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Correction of malrotation by lysis of duodenal bands and/or reduction of midgut volvulus (eg, Ladd procedure)
pairs.concern: Ladd procedure inherently includes lysis/reduction work; surgeons may document adhesiolysis, but separate 44005 payment should be suppressed.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Correction of malrotation by lysis of duodenal bands and/or reduction of midgut volvulus (eg, Ladd procedure)
pairs.column2Description: Exploratory laparotomy, exploratory celiotomy with or without biopsy(s)
pairs.concern: Known issue case; exploration is inherent to the Ladd/laparotomy operation and should be suppressed.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.concern: Trauma splenectomy may involve adhesiolysis in prior-operation abdomen; legitimate work may be documented but 44005 is bundled.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Laparoscopy, surgical, esophagogastroduodenoscopy fundoplasty (eg, Nissen, Toupet procedures)
pairs.rationale: Misuse of Column Two code with Column One code
pairs.concern: Foregut fundoplication in reoperative abdomen can involve adhesiolysis; suppression is correct but may need clear explanation.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Laparoscopy, surgical, repair of paraesophageal hernia
pairs.rationale: Misuse of Column Two code with Column One code
pairs.concern: Paraesophageal hernia repair commonly involves mediastinal/abdominal dissection; separate enterolysis can be confusing.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Laparoscopy, surgical, gastric restrictive procedure; Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
pairs.rationale: Misuse of Column Two code with Column One code
pairs.concern: Bariatric bypass with adhesiolysis is a common surgeon-reported combination; NCCI modifier-0 suppresses 44005.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.concern: Sleeve gastrectomy with adhesiolysis may be documented; risk is user expectation that adhesiolysis adds payable wRVU.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Hepatectomy, resection of liver; partial lobectomy
pairs.concern: Hepatectomy with adhesiolysis in reoperative upper abdomen can be real work; payable suppression should be explicit.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.

pairs.column1Description: Direct repair of aneurysm, abdominal aorta
pairs.concern: Open abdominal vascular exposure/AAA repair can require adhesiolysis; vascular users may expect separate reporting but NCCI suppresses.
pairs.recommendation: Keep in 159-pair activation, but monitor post-deploy search/report feedback and keep warning-card text explicit.
